was: Shasta-Trinity NF campground on the upper Trinity River near the Eagle Creek confluence, Hwy 3 north of Trinity Center, 17-18 sites, drinking water, vault toilets, RVs/trailers to 35 ft; open roughly mid-May to late August. --Claude

was: Inyo NF campground ~2 mi from Mammoth Lakes along aspen-lined Sherwin Creek (elev ~7,600 ft); 87 sites, RVs to 60 ft (most 35-40), no hookups, water, vault toilets, RV fill station, bear lockers; Sherwin Lakes trailhead adjacent. Reservable, open ~mid-May to early Sep. --Claude

was: Family-owned RV park & campground on the shore of Bridgeport Reservoir off Hwy 182, Eastern Sierra. Full-hookup drive-in RV sites plus a few tent sites and rental trailers; restrooms/showers, laundry, dump station; typically a 2-3 night minimum in season (5 over the 4th of July), none on same-day bookings. Blue-ribbon trout fishing (reservoir + East Walker River). --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: typically 2-3 nights in season, 5 over the 4th of July; none on same-day bookings (paradiseshorescamp.com, 2026-10-12). --Claude

was: Family campground on Hwy 60 at Dwight, about 20 km west of Algonquin Provincial Park's West Gate and 23 km from Huntsville. Listed at 143 drive-in sites — 43 pull-throughs, 15 full-hookup and 98 hydro/water sites on 15/30 amp — plus glamping tents and a cabin. Washroom/shower buildings, coin laundry, camp store, dump station, pool, mini-putt, playground and covered pavilion. Open Victoria Day long weekend to Thanksgiving. --Claude

was: Small owner-operated RV park on Bushwell Bay off the North Channel of Georgian Bay (Lake Huron), east of Spanish. 42 sites, all with metered 30/50-amp hydro, water and full sewer (pump-out); back-ins listed to 50 ft; shaded, sunny and water-front sites plus limited boat dockage. Site mix is mostly leased seasonal, but the operator's rate sheet explicitly lists 'transient sites available' with 30/50-amp hydro and water at $60-80 CAD daily ($360-480 weekly), so nightly RV camping is a standing product. No tents allowed; RV/trailer units older than 15 years may be refused. Open early May to mid-October (Thanksgiving). Book by phone/email reservation form; no online booking engine. --Claude

was: 40-acre partially wooded campground on Lake Louise, on Hwy 129 about 20 km (15 minutes) south of Chapleau. Over 50 full-service sites offered for overnight, weekly or seasonal use, all with drinking water, 30-50 amp electric, septic, fire pit and picnic table; drive-through sites suit motorhomes and trailers, plus tent areas and housekeeping cabins. Renovated shower house, game room, camp shop, playground, private sandy beach with paddle boats, kayaks, SUPs and a floating trampoline; ATV and logging-road trails from the property. Open mid-May to mid-October, weather permitting; reserve by phone or email. --Claude

was: 226 gravel-pad sites on McGowan Lake at 21321 Highway 7, Maberly, in Lanark County; mix of seasonal and overnight camping. Unserviced, premium unserviced (water only), 15-amp serviced, 30-amp serviced; maximum of four adults. Sandy beach, store, laundry, showers, dump station, two playgrounds, dog park, rec hall. Open May 1 to Oct 1; credit card holds a reservation, 48-hour cancellation. --Claude

was: Family-run park in the hamlet of Red Bay on the Bruce Peninsula, 428 Huron Rd. 75 sites total — 55 seasonal plus a transient block of 8 overnight serviced RV sites, 5 overnight tent sites and 5 unserviced wilderness sites. Serviced sites are 30 amp hydro, sewer and potable water; max RV length 34 ft. 2026 overnight rates $55/night wilderness (3-night minimum on long weekends, $10 reservation fee). Open early May to Thanksgiving (approx May 7 - Oct 11). Reserve by email/phone with a one-night non-refundable deposit. --Claude

was: Long-running family park (in operation over 90 years) on the east shore of Little Lake in Midland, minutes from town. 147 sites split between a fully-booked seasonal section and an overnight section; the operator's site map shows numbered loops on Stan's Circle, Minnow/Catfish/Perch/Bass Drives and Lakeshore Road with 30-amp and 50-amp electric, water and sewer, paved roads and gravel pads, plus pull-thrus.  No tent camping.  Beach on Little Lake, pool, store, propane, laundry, playground.  Overnight season runs mid-May to October; reservations through CampLife.  A separate mobile-home park adjoins the campground at the office end. --Claude

Washrooms/showers, dump station; cell reception extremely limited. Reservable, open ~late June to early Sept. --Claude

The 30-amp full-service sites are for RVs only, pull-through or back-in, to 70 ft; the 15-amp and unserviced lake-view sites take tents or RVs to 40 ft, back-in only, and the wooded unserviced sites RVs to 20 ft, and there is a group site. --Claude

was: Town of Musgrave Harbour municipal park ~8 km south of town on Rte 330 (Kittiwake Coast), on a saltwater pond beside an ocean beach. 50/30-amp power+water and water-only drive-in sites; comfort station with washrooms, showers and laundromat; dump station; interpretation centre, playground, walking trail. Seasonal sites available; open ~mid-Jun to early Sep. Named for Sir Frederick Banting. --Claude

was: Family-owned campground on the North Fork Holston River about 5 miles from Abingdon and the Virginia Creeper Trail. Operator's site lists 94 full-hookup sites (30/50 amp, pull-thrus available) taken for overnight, monthly and permanent stays, plus 22-38 20-amp electric/water sites for tents and pop-ups; posted single-night rates are $35 tent (6 nights get the 7th free). Season runs April 1 to October 31; a seasonal site is $1,650/year plus metered electric, so the park mixes seasonals with a real nightly inventory. Pool, bathhouse, laundry, camp store, propane. Reservations by phone; specific sites are not guaranteed. --Claude

was: Primitive drive-in campground on the South Fork Shenandoah River. No hookups: picnic table and fire ring per site, portable toilets serviced weekly, generators permitted, self-contained campers and RVs explicitly allowed; grass sites reached by a gravel drive along the riverbank. 17 sites the operator calls riverfront plus others with river access, and a large area for groups of 25+. 50% deposit at booking. Drive-ups accepted April 1 to October 1 and sites reservable by phone year round. Quiet time from midnight to 8 AM which is late by campground standards, so music can run well into the night. --Claude

was: Family-owned campground on the Clinch River about 7 miles off the main highway near Duffield. Operator lists 27 full-hookup sites, 20 premium full-hookup sites on the river and 11 electric/water sites, plus 11 rustic tent sites on the riverbank; level gravel pads, 30 amp standard with limited 50 amp, big-rig friendly, boat launch, renovated bathhouse, fire pit and picnic table per site, Wi-Fi. Open year round. Rustic tent $25, E/W tent $35; weekly, monthly and long-term sites also offered. Reservable online, or by phone/text. --Claude

was: Family-run (Runkle family) campground at 2084 Wharton Rd (Route 872) in Wharton Twp, southern Potter County, strung along the First Fork of Sinnemahoning Creek; RV Life counts 123 sites. The operator's campground map splits them explicitly: roughly 30 blue "Reservable RV Sites" numbered 1-33 with water and 30-amp electric, a much larger brown seasonal RV block numbered 100-196, 11 tent sites and 6 rental cabins. Published nightly rates are $30 primitive tent / $35 deluxe tent, cabins $80-120. Two catch-and-release ponds, camp store with live bait and propane, two dump stations, gem mining. Reservable online through the operator's own booking page; the operator site does not publish opening or closing dates. --Claude

was: Long-established family campground at 1077 Blue Mountain Dr in Bangor (Slate Belt, ~20 min from the Delaware Water Gap NRA); RV Life counts 138 sites. The operator's 2025 site map shows roughly 130 numbered full-hookup pads on several loops around an on-site stocked lake, plus about 25 tent sites, two rental cabins and a rental RV; pool, camp store, laundry, game room, dump station and propane. Season runs April 11 to October 18, with the operator publishing a nightly water & electric campsite rate (6 nights and the 7th free) alongside seasonal ($2,350 for 2 nights/week) and all-season ($3,400 for 22 weeks) packages. The seasonal contingent is large - golf carts are restricted to seasonal campers and gate cards are issued to seasonal families - so transient sites are limited; reserve by phone or the site's inquiry form (no online booking engine). --Claude
